title: CharmOS nightmare suite
description: Schema for CharmOS nightmare stress-test suite configuration files. A suite definition contains three sections: 'suite' specifies orchestrator scheduling parameters, 'build' specifies the kernel build configuration used by all tasks, and 'tasks' defines the individual test campaigns executed by runners.

name.description: Lowercase identifier (starts with a letter, contains only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, max 64 characters) compatible with kernel command-line arguments without quoting.

service.description: Name of a harness perturbation service.

suite.description: Suite-level orchestrator scheduling and budget parameters.

runners.description: Maximum number of concurrent runners the orchestrator may allocate to this suite.

budget_hours.description: Total wall-clock execution budget for the suite, in hours.

overlap_ratio.description: Fraction of the total suite budget reserved for overlapping runner handoffs during campaign transitions.

build.description: Kernel build configuration shared across all tasks in the suite, including compiler, build type, CMake definitions, SMP topology, and memory size.

compiler.description: C compiler toolchain used for the build ('gcc' or 'clang'). 'clang' is required when enabling DEBUG_ASAN (KASAN).

cmake_definitions.description: List of CMake cache variable definitions to pass to the build.

items.description: CMake cache variable definition in KEY=VALUE format, passed to CMake as -DKEY=VALUE.

smp.description: SMP (symmetric multiprocessing) CPU topology for QEMU.

cores.description: Number of CPU cores per socket.

threads.description: Number of hardware threads per core.

memory_mib.description: Guest RAM size in megabytes (MiB) allocated to QEMU.

name.description: Name of the nightmare test subject to execute. Passed to the guest kernel command line as 'nightmare=<name>'.

mode.description: Execution mode for the task campaign: 'horizontal' distributes distinct PRNG seeds across concurrent runners; 'vertical' executes a single extended sequence of boots on one runner.

weight.description: Relative weight used by the scheduler to allocate the suite's time budget among tasks.

priority.description: Scheduling priority for task admission when runner capacity is constrained (higher values are scheduled first).

max_runners.description: Maximum number of concurrent runners allocated to this task. Defaults to the suite-level runner limit.

boot.description: Execution and timeout parameters for individual VM boot cycles. Deadlines are hierarchical: duration_ms is the guest soft run duration, drain_grace_ms is the additional time allowed for graceful quiescence before the guest hard deadline, and timeout_ms is the host watchdog kill deadline.

duration_ms.description: Soft run duration per boot in milliseconds. When this duration expires, the test harness signals NM_STOP_BUDGET, initiates quiescence, and collects test results.

drain_grace_ms.description: Grace period in milliseconds allowed for services to quiesce after the soft duration expires. If the guest fails to finish within this window, the harness emits a stall verdict ('result=stall reason=drain_timeout') and terminates the VM.

timeout_ms.description: Host-enforced hard timeout per boot in milliseconds, after which the host process terminates the QEMU instance. Zero selects the derived default: duration_ms + drain_grace_ms + 15000ms. Any explicit non-zero value must exceed the guest hard deadline (duration_ms + drain_grace_ms) by at least the serial flush margin.

gate_first.description: Whether to run standard kernel sanity/gate tests before starting the stress campaign. If true, gate test failures abort the run immediately without proceeding to perturbation.

max_boots.description: Maximum number of VM boot cycles permitted for this task, preventing repeated early crashes from consuming the entire time budget in a reboot loop.

min_interval_ms.description: Minimum elapsed time in milliseconds required between consecutive boot starts to throttle reboot loops after rapid crashes.

stat_interval_ms.description: Interval in milliseconds between guest heartbeat and statistics log emissions.

stall_threshold_ms.description: Liveness stall detection threshold in milliseconds.

on_stall.description: Action taken when aggregate Nightmare progress stalls: 'report' emits a finding and attempts bounded cooperative teardown, and 'crash' emits the finding and enters the kernel crash path.

nightmare.description: Nightmare harness configuration, controlling perturbation intensity, PRNG seeding strategy, and active perturbation services.

intensity.description: Overall perturbation intensity scale from 0.0 (minimal/no perturbation) to 1.0 (maximum perturbation), passed to the kernel as a fixed-point value.

seed_mode.description: PRNG seed distribution strategy: 'split' seeds perturbation services deterministically while allowing the test subject to run unseeded; 'seedful' deterministically seeds both perturbation services and the test subject; 'seedless' seeds neither. The kernel validates that this setting satisfies the test subject's declared seed_policy.

perturb.description: List of harness perturbation services to enable for this task. Each named service will be activated during the run.

perturb_opts.description: Configuration options for individual perturbation services, keyed by service name. Each configured service must also be listed in 'perturb'.

opts.description: Subject-specific test configuration parameters, passed to the kernel command line as 'nightmare.<task_name>.<key>=<value>'.
